Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on first person pronouns?
Comment: Copulative clause described as intransitive: "ŋa tɛ katɕhi ʂʅ o" - I am really happy
curated: corrected: identity Lisu; evidence replaced; verified 1
curated_comment: Identity corrected: source = Yu 2007 (Lisu); glottocode -> lisu1250 (was ning1281='Ninglang', a Lisu dialect); name 'Anong' (=nung1282) was wrong. The original evidence ('pa te katshi si o' = 'I am happy') was INAPPROPRIATE: intransitive 1SG with te (patient-S/absolutive side), not ergative A. DECISIVE evidence found: ex.88 (p.130) 'ga le ... [count]' glossed 1SG.A -- 1st person pronoun ga takes the agentive marker le as transitive A. Lisu (Yu 2007 sec.4.2, pp.82-83) has split-S/agentive (semantic) flagging: an OPTIONAL agentive marker le (= ni in Nujiang/Ninglang/Dechang, tche in Lipo) flags A and, for emphasis, agentive-S (Sa); an OPTIONAL object marker te (= the in Lipo) flags O and patient-S (Sp). Marking favored when an object is present / for disambiguation. NOTE: this is the agentive 'ergative-side' marker, not canonical ergative-absolutive (le also reaches Sa), so coding 1 reflects the agentive/split-S pattern under the existential reading; downgrade if the project requires A-only ergative.
